[[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Tumulus}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal shape. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Tumulus Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Cultural Properties == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal shape. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Cultural Properties == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal shape. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Cultural Properties == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal shape. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Cultural Properties == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal shape. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Cultural Properties == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya It is designated as a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal shape. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Cultural Properties == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal shape. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Cultural Properties == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} ---- {{Short description|Ancient tomb in Japan}} {{Draft topics|east-asia}} {{AfC topic|geo}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳}}|image= File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-3.jpg |name = Mitsuya Kofun (三津屋古墳) |image = [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu door.jpg|280px]]
Kofun and stone chamber entrance |所在地 = {{ill|Yoshioka, Gunma|ja|吉岡町}}, Gunma Prefecture |coordinates = Ōkubō 2037-1, Mitsuya |緯度度 = 36|緯度分 = 26|緯度秒 = 6.15 |経度度 = 139|経度分 = 1|経度秒 = 32.52 |形状 = {{ill|Octagonal tumulus|ja|八角墳}} |規模 = Diagonal length: 23.8m
Height: 4.5m |埋葬施設 = Bilateral entry {{ill|Horizontal stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} |築造時期 = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |史跡 = Gunma Prefectural Historic Site |地図 = Japan Gunma }} '''Mitsuya Kofun''' (三津屋古墳) is an {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳}} located in {{ill|Yoshioka, Gunma|ja|吉岡町}}, Gunma Prefecture. It is designated as a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is an {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳}}.{{Cite web |date=2015-09-07 |title=Mitsuya Kofun [三津屋古墳] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=31732 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150907095743/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=31732 |archive-date=2015-09-07 }} A rare kind of tomb mostly reserved for 7th century [[Emperor of Japan|Emperors of Japan]].{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}}{{Cite web |title=Gobyōyama Kofun (in Kyōto) |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21}}[[Emperor Jomei|i]]{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 |access-date=2023-10-20}}.{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Kofun, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Kofun |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal Kofun said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}}, The inner chamber is open to the public. unlike many other Kofun which are strictly restricted by the [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal shape. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Cultural Properties == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: Designated on March 24, 1995; expanded on March 23, 2001. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|Sources used in article preparation}} * Mitsuya Kofun Explanatory Signboard [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal shape. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Cultural Properties == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} ---- {{Short description|Ancient tomb in Japan}} {{Draft topics|east-asia}} {{AfC topic|geo}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳}}|image= File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-3.jpg |name = Mitsuya Kofun (三津屋古墳) |image = [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu door.jpg|280px]]
Kofun and stone chamber entrance |所在地 = {{ill|Yoshioka, Gunma|ja|吉岡町}}, Gunma Prefecture |coordinates = Ōkubō 2037-1, Mitsuya |緯度度 = 36|緯度分 = 26|緯度秒 = 6.15 |経度度 = 139|経度分 = 1|経度秒 = 32.52 |形状 = {{ill|Octagonal tumulus|ja|八角墳}} |規模 = Diagonal length: 23.8m
Height: 4.5m |埋葬施設 = Bilateral entry {{ill|Horizontal stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} |築造時期 = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |史跡 = Gunma Prefectural Historic Site |地図 = Japan Gunma }} '''Mitsuya Kofun''' (三津屋古墳) is an {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳}} located in {{ill|Yoshioka, Gunma|ja|吉岡町}}, Gunma Prefecture. It is designated as a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is an {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳}}.{{Cite web |date=2015-09-07 |title=Mitsuya Kofun [三津屋古墳] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=31732 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150907095743/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=31732 |archive-date=2015-09-07 }} A rare kind of tomb mostly reserved for 7th century [[Emperor of Japan|Emperors of Japan]].{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}}{{Cite web |title=Gobyōyama Kofun (in Kyōto) |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21}}[[Emperor Jomei|i]]{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 |access-date=2023-10-20}}.{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Kofun, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Kofun |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal Kofun said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}}, The inner chamber is open to the public. unlike many other Kofun which are strictly restricted by the [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal shape. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Cultural Properties == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal shape. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Cultural Properties == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal shape. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Cultural Properties == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya It is designated as a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is an {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳}}.{{Cite web |date=2015-09-07 |title=Mitsuya Kofun [三津屋古墳] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=31732 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150907095743/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=31732 |archive-date=2015-09-07 }} A rare kind of tomb mostly reserved for 7th century [[Emperor of Japan|Emperors of Japan]].{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}}{{Cite web |title=Gobyōyama Kofun (in Kyōto) |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21}}[[Emperor Jomei|i]]{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal Kofun said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal shape. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Cultural Properties == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal shape. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Cultural Properties == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun and stone chamber entrance |所在地 = {{ill|Yoshioka, Gunma|ja|吉岡町}}, Gunma Prefecture |coordinates = Ōkubō 2037-1, Mitsuya |緯度度 = 36|緯度分 = 26|緯度秒 = 6.15 |経度度 = 139|経度分 = 1|経度秒 = 32.52 |type = {{ill|Octagonal tumulus|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}} |規模 = Diagonal length: 23.8m
Height: 4.5m |埋葬施設 = Bilateral entry {{ill|Horizontal stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} |築造時期 = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |史跡 = Gunma Prefectural Historic Site |地図 = Japan Gunma }} '''Mitsuya Kofun''' (三津屋古墳) is an {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}} located in {{ill|Yoshioka, Gunma|ja|吉岡町}}, Gunma Prefecture. It is designated as a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is an {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}}.{{Cite web |date=2015-09-07 |title=Mitsuya Kofun [三津屋古墳] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=31732 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150907095743/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=31732 |archive-date=2015-09-07 }} A rare kind of tomb mostly reserved for 7th century [[Emperor of Japan|Emperors of Japan]].{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}}{{Cite web |title=Gobyōyama Kofun (in Kyōto) |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21}}[[Emperor Jomei|i]]{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 |access-date=2023-10-20}}.{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Kofun, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Kofun |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal Kofun said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}}, The inner chamber is open to the public. unlike many other Kofun which are strictly restricted by the [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal shape. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Cultural Properties == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal shape. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Cultural Properties == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal shape. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Cultural Properties == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal shape. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Cultural Properties == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Specifically, it is an {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}}.{{Cite web |date=2015-09-07 |title=Mitsuya Kofun [三津屋古墳] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal shape. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Cultural Properties == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal shape. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Cultural Properties == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal shape. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Cultural Properties == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya I'd suggest expanding the article and making sure the references are relevant before resubmitting. [[User:Turnagra|Turnagra]] ([[User talk:Turnagra|talk]]) 02:32, 12 November 2023 (UTC)}} ---- {{Short description|Ancient tomb in Japan}} {{Draft topics|east-asia}} {{AfC topic|geo}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}}|image= File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-3.jpg |name = Mitsuya Kofun (三津屋古墳) |image = [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu door.jpg|280px]]
Kofun and stone chamber entrance |所在地 = {{ill|Yoshioka, Gunma|ja|吉岡町}}, Gunma Prefecture |coordinates = Ōkubō 2037-1, Mitsuya |緯度度 = 36|緯度分 = 26|緯度秒 = 6.15 |経度度 = 139|経度分 = 1|経度秒 = 32.52 |type = {{ill|Octagonal tumulus|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}} |規模 = Diagonal length: 23.8m
Height: 4.5m |埋葬施設 = Bilateral entry {{ill|Horizontal stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} |築造時期 = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |史跡 = Gunma Prefectural Historic Site |地図 = Japan Gunma }} '''Mitsuya Kofun''' (三津屋古墳) is an {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}} located in {{ill|Yoshioka, Gunma|ja|吉岡町}}, Gunma Prefecture. It is designated as a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is an {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}}.{{Cite web |date=2015-09-07 |title=Mitsuya Kofun [三津屋古墳] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=31732 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150907095743/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=31732 |archive-date=2015-09-07 }} A rare kind of tomb mostly reserved for 7th century [[Emperor of Japan|Emperors of Japan]].{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}}{{Cite web |title=Gobyōyama Kofun (in Kyōto) |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21}}[[Emperor Jomei|i]]{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 |access-date=2023-10-20}}.{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Kofun, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Kofun |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal Kofun said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}}, The inner chamber is open to the public. unlike many other Kofun which are strictly restricted by the [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal shape. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Cultural Properties == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal shape. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Cultural Properties == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Cultural Properties == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == other_designation == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: Kofun and stone chamber entrance |所在地 = {{ill|Yoshioka, Gunma|ja|吉岡町}}, Gunma Prefecture |coordinates = Ōkubō 2037-1, Mitsuya |緯度度 = 36|緯度分 = 26|緯度秒 = 6.15 |経度度 = 139|経度分 = 1|経度秒 = 32.52 |type = {{ill|Octagonal tumulus|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}} |規模 = Diagonal length: 23.8m
Height: 4.5m |埋葬施設 = Bilateral entry {{ill|Horizontal stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} |築造時期 = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |史跡 = Gunma Prefectural Historic Site |地図 = Japan Gunma }} '''Mitsuya Kofun''' (三津屋古墳) is an {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}} located in {{ill|Yoshioka, Gunma|ja|吉岡町}}, Gunma Prefecture. It is designated as a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is an {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}}.{{Cite web |date=2015-09-07 |title=Mitsuya Kofun [三津屋古墳] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=31732 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150907095743/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=31732 |archive-date=2015-09-07 }} A rare kind of tomb mostly reserved for 7th century [[Emperor of Japan|Emperors of Japan]].{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}}{{Cite web |title=Gobyōyama Kofun (in Kyōto) |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21}}[[Emperor Jomei|i]]{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 |access-date=2023-10-20}}.{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Kofun, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Kofun |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal Kofun said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}}, The inner chamber is open to the public. unlike many other Kofun which are strictly restricted by the [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == other_designation == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == other_designation == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == other_designation == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == other_designation == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == other_designation == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == other_designation == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural other_designation. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == other_designation == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * other_designation ''' Mitsuya [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural other_designation. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == other_designation == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * other_designation ''' Mitsuya [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural other_designation. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == other_designation == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * other_designation ''' Mitsuya
