[[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designated a Gunma Prefectural other_designation. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == other_designation == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * other_designation ''' Mitsuya [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall forming an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was designation1 a Gunma Prefectural other_designation. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == other_designation == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * other_designation ''' Mitsuya Kofun and stone chamber entrance |location = {{ill|Yoshioka, Gunma|ja|吉岡町}}, Gunma Prefecture |coordinates = Ōkubō 2037-1, Mitsuya |緯度度 = 36|緯度分 = 26|緯度秒 = 6.15 |経度度 = 139|経度分 = 1|経度秒 = 32.52 |type = {{ill|Octagonal tumulus|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}} |area = Diagonal length: 23.8m
Height: 4.5m |埋葬施設 = Bilateral entry {{ill|Horizontal stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} |築造時期 = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |史跡 = Gunma Prefectural other_other_designation |地図 = Japan Gunma }} '''Mitsuya Kofun''' (三津屋古墳) is an {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}} located in {{ill|Yoshioka, Gunma|ja|吉岡町}}, Gunma Prefecture. It is other_designation1 as a Gunma Prefectural other_other_designation. {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is an {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}}.{{Cite web |date=2015-09-07 |title=Mitsuya Kofun [三津屋古墳] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=31732 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150907095743/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=31732 |archive-date=2015-09-07 }} A rare kind of tomb mostly reserved for 7th century [[Emperor of Japan|Emperors of Japan]].{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}}{{Cite web |title=Gobyōyama Kofun (in Kyōto) |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21}}[[Emperor Jomei|i]]{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 |access-date=2023-10-20}}.{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Kofun, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Kofun |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal Kofun said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}}, The inner chamber is open to the public. unlike many other Kofun which are strictly restricted by the [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was other_designation1 a Gunma Prefectural other_other_designation. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == other_other_designation == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * other_other_designation [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was other_designation1 a Gunma Prefectural other_other_designation. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == other_other_designation == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * other_other_designation [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was other_designation1 a Gunma Prefectural other_other_designation. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == other_other_designation == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * other_other_designation [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was other_designation1 a Gunma Prefectural other_designation. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was other_designation1 a Gunma Prefectural other_designation. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == other_designation == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * other_designation ''' Mitsuya [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was other_designation1 a Gunma Prefectural other_designation. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == other_designation == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * other_designation ''' Mitsuya [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was other_designation1 a Gunma Prefectural other_designation. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == other_designation == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * other_designation ''' Mitsuya [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was other_designation1 a Gunma Prefectural other_designation. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == other_designation == === Gunma Prefectural Designation === * other_designation ''' Mitsuya Kofun and stone chamber entrance |location = {{ill|Yoshioka, Gunma|ja|吉岡町}}, Gunma Prefecture |coordinates = Ōkubō 2037-1, Mitsuya |緯度度 = 36|緯度分 = 26|緯度秒 = 6.15 |経度度 = 139|経度分 = 1|経度秒 = 32.52 |type = {{ill|Octagonal tumulus|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}} |area = Diagonal length: 23.8m
Height: 4.5m |埋葬施設 = Bilateral entry {{ill|Horizontal stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} |築造時期 = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |史跡 = Gunma Prefectural other_designation |地図 = Japan Gunma }} '''Mitsuya Kofun''' (三津屋古墳) is an {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}} located in {{ill|Yoshioka, Gunma|ja|吉岡町}}, Gunma Prefecture. It is other_designation1 as a Gunma Prefectural other_designation. {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is an {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}}.{{Cite web |date=2015-09-07 |title=Mitsuya Kofun [三津屋古墳] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=31732 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150907095743/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=31732 |archive-date=2015-09-07 }} A rare kind of tomb mostly reserved for 7th century [[Emperor of Japan|Emperors of Japan]].{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}}{{Cite web |title=Gobyōyama Kofun (in Kyōto) |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21}}[[Emperor Jomei|i]]{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 |access-date=2023-10-20}}.{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Kofun, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Kofun |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal Kofun said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}}, The inner chamber is open to the public. unlike many other Kofun which are strictly restricted by the [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was other_designation1 a Gunma Prefectural other_designation. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == other_designation == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * other_designation ''' Mitsuya [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was other_designation1 a Gunma Prefectural other_designation. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == other_designation == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * other_designation ''' Mitsuya [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was other_designation1 a Gunma Prefectural other_designation. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == other_designation == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * other_designation ''' Mitsuya River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was other_designation1 a Gunma Prefectural other_designation. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == other_designation == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * other_designation ''' Mitsuya [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was other_designation1 a Gunma Prefectural other_designation. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == other_designation == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * other_designation ''' Mitsuya Kofun and stone chamber entrance |location = {{ill|Yoshioka, Gunma|ja|吉岡町}}, Gunma Prefecture |coordinates = Ōkubō 2037-1, Mitsuya |緯度度 = 36|緯度分 = 26|緯度秒 = 6.15 |経度度 = 139|経度分 = 1|経度秒 = 32.52 |type = {{ill|Octagonal tumulus|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}} |area = Diagonal length: 23.8m
Height: 4.5m |埋葬施設 = Bilateral entry {{ill|Horizontal stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} |築造時期 = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |史跡 = Gunma Prefectural other_designation |地図 = Japan Gunma }} '''Mitsuya Kofun''' (三津屋古墳) is an {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}} located in {{ill|Yoshioka, Gunma|ja|吉岡町}}, Gunma Prefecture. It is other_designation1 as a Gunma Prefectural other_designation. {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is an {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}}.{{Cite web |date=2015-09-07 |title=Mitsuya Kofun [三津屋古墳] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=31732 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150907095743/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=31732 |archive-date=2015-09-07 }} A rare kind of tomb mostly reserved for 7th century [[Emperor of Japan|Emperors of Japan]].{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}}{{Cite web |title=Gobyōyama Kofun (in Kyōto) |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21}}[[Emperor Jomei|i]]{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 |access-date=2023-10-20}}.{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Kofun, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Kofun |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal Kofun said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}}, The inner chamber is open to the public. unlike many other Kofun which are strictly restricted by the [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was other_designation1 a Gunma Prefectural other_designation. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == other_designation == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * other_designation ''' Mitsuya [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was other_designation1 a Gunma Prefectural other_designation. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == other_designation == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * other_designation ''' Mitsuya [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was other_designation1 a Gunma Prefectural other_designation. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == other_designation == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * other_designation ''' Mitsuya [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: [[Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|ja|榛名山}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Tennōryō Kofun|ja|天皇陵|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. {{日本の古墳 |名称 = 三津屋古墳 |画像 = [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu door.jpg|280px]]
墳丘・石室開口部 |別名 = |所属 = |所在地 = [[群馬県]][[北群馬郡]][[吉岡町]]大字大久保2037-1（字三津屋） |緯度度 = 36|緯度分 = 26|緯度秒 = 6.15 |経度度 = 139|経度分 = 1|経度秒 = 32.52 |ISO = JP-10 |形状 = [[八角墳]] |規模 = 対角長23.8m
高さ4.5m |埋葬施設 = 両袖式[[横穴式石室]] |出土品 = |陪塚 = |築造時期 = [[7世紀]]後半 |被葬者 = |陵墓 = |史跡 = 群馬県指定史跡「三津屋古墳」 |有形文化財 = |特記事項 = |地図 = Japan Gunma |アイコン = 八角墳 |ラベル = 三津屋古墳 |ラベル位置 = top }} '''三津屋古墳'''（みつやこふん）は、[[群馬県]][[北群馬郡]][[吉岡町]]大久保にある[[古墳]]。形状は[[八角墳]]。群馬県指定史跡に指定されている。 == 概要 == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|墳丘}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|石室}}]] 群馬県中部、[[榛名山]]東麓において、[[利根川]]に注ぐ午王頭川の左岸に築造された古墳である。これまでに石室は大きく破壊を受けているほか、[[1993年]]（[[平成]]5年）に発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は正八角形{{Sfn|三津屋古墳（平凡社、刊行後版）|2006}}。墳丘は2段築成で、厚さ10センチメートル程度の[[版築]]状の水平積み上げによって構築される{{Sfn|三津屋古墳（平凡社、刊行後版）|2006}}。墳丘外表には[[葺石]]が認められるほか、墳丘周囲には周濠が巡らされる。埋葬施設は両袖式の[[横穴式石室]]で、玄室奥壁を八角形の中心として南方向に開口する。石室は大きく破壊を受けているが、自然石乱石積みによって構築されて一部には切石を使用したと見られ、前面には前庭部を付す{{Sfn|三津屋古墳（平凡社、刊行後版）|2006}}。盗掘のため副葬品は詳らかでない。 この三津屋古墳は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]後半頃の築造と推定される。八角墳は[[段ノ塚古墳]]（[[奈良県]][[桜井市]]、[[舒明天皇]]陵）・[[御廟野古墳]]（[[京都府]][[京都市]]、[[天智天皇]]陵）・[[野口王墓|野口王墓古墳]]（奈良県[[明日香村]]、[[天武天皇|天武]]・[[持統天皇]]合葬陵）など当時の[[天皇陵]]クラスの古墳で採用される墳丘形態であり、当地の豪族の特異性を示す点で貴重な古墳になる。また本古墳の北西にある[[南下古墳群]]は上毛野地域において総社古墳群（[[前橋市]]）に次ぐ有力首長墓群であり、本古墳と合わせて畿内[[ヤマト王権]]による上毛野地域の中央集権化との関係を考察するうえで重要視される右島和夫「記念講演 古墳から見た七世紀の上毛野地域 -吉岡町南下古墳群を中心として-」『群馬文化』第338号、群馬県地域文化研究協議会、2019年。。 古墳域は[[1995年]]（平成7年）に群馬県指定史跡に指定されている。 == 遺跡歴 == * [[1993年]]（[[平成]]5年）、発掘調査（吉岡町教育委員会、[[1996年]]に報告書刊行）。 * [[1995年]]（平成7年）3月24日、群馬県指定史跡に指定。 * [[2001年]]（平成13年）3月23日、史跡範囲の追加指定。 == 墳丘 == 古墳の規模は、対角長約23.8メートル・残存高さ4.5メートルを測り、八角形の一辺は下段約9メートル・上段約6メートルを測る。築造に際しては1尺約30センチメートルの唐尺の使用が推測される。 墳丘の葺石には、下段では山石が、上段では扁平な川原石が使用されており、特に上段は精巧な造りになる。 == 文化財 == === 群馬県指定文化財 === * 史跡 ** 三津屋古墳 - 1995年（平成7年）3月24日指定、2001年（平成13年）3月23日追加指定[https://www.net.yoshioka.ed.jp/%e6%8c%87%e5%ae%9a%e6%96%87%e5%8c%96%e8%b2%a1/%e4%b8%89%e6%b4%a5%e5%b1%8b%e5%8f%a4%e5%a2%b3 三津屋古墳]（吉岡町教育委員会）。史跡説明板。。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用した文献）}} * 史跡説明板（吉岡町教育委員会、2021年設置） * [http://www.net.yoshioka.ed.jp/%E5%90%89%E5%B2%A1%E7%94%BA%E6%96%87%E5%8C%96%E8%B2%A1%E3%82%BB%E3%83%B3%E3%82%BF%E3%83%BC-1/%E3%83%91%E3%83%B3%E3%83%95%E3%83%AC%E3%83%83%E3%83%88%E3%83%BB%E5%8B%95%E7%94%BB/?action=common_download_main&upload_id=4439 三津屋古墳パンフレット]（吉岡町教育委員会、2021年） - リンクは吉岡町教育委員会。 * {{Cite book|和書|author1=大塚初重|authorlink1=大塚初重|author2=柳下恵理子|year=|chapter=三津屋古墳|title=[[日本大百科全書]]（ニッポニカ）|publisher=[[小学館]]|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|三津屋古墳（日本大百科全書）}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=荒木勇次|year=2002|chapter=三津屋古墳|title=[[日本古墳大辞典|続 日本古墳大辞典]]|publisher=[[東京堂出版]]|isbn=4490105991|ref={{Harvid|三津屋古墳（続古墳）|2002}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=2006|chapter=三津屋古墳|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 10 群馬県の地名 刊行後版（[[ジャパンナレッジ]]収録）|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=4582490107|ref={{Harvid|三津屋古墳（平凡社、刊行後版）|2006}}}} == 関連文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用していない関連文献）}} * {{Cite book|和書|year=1996|title=三津屋古墳 -八角形墳の調査-（吉岡町文化財調査報告書 第7集）|publisher=吉岡町教育委員会|ref=}} == 関連項目 == * [[南下古墳群]] * [[三宮神社 (吉岡町)]] == 外部リンク == {{Commonscat|Mitsuya Kofun}} * [https://www.net.yoshioka.ed.jp/%e6%8c%87%e5%ae%9a%e6%96%87%e5%8c%96%e8%b2%a1/%e4%b8%89%e6%b4%a5%e5%b1%8b%e5%8f%a4%e5%a2%b3 三津屋古墳] - 吉岡町教育委員会 {{デフォルトソート:みつやこふん}} [[Category:群馬県の古墳]] [[Category:吉岡町の歴史]] [[Category:八角墳]] [[Category:群馬県指定史跡]]

高さ4.5m |埋葬施設 = 両袖式[[横穴式石室]] |出土品 = |陪塚 = |築造時期 = [[7世紀]]後半 |被葬者 = |陵墓 = |史跡 = 群馬県指定史跡「三津屋古墳」 |有形文化財 = |特記事項 = |地図 = Japan Gunma |アイコン = 八角墳 |ラベル = 三津屋古墳 |ラベル位置 = top }} '''三津屋古墳'''（みつやこふん）は、[[群馬県]][[北群馬郡]][[吉岡町]]大久保にある[[古墳]]。形状は[[八角墳]]。群馬県指定史跡に指定されている。 == 概要 == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|墳丘}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|石室}}]] 群馬県中部、[[榛名山]]東麓において、[[利根川]]に注ぐ午王頭川の左岸に築造された古墳である。これまでに石室は大きく破壊を受けているほか、[[1993年]]（[[平成]]5年）に発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は正八角形{{Sfn|三津屋古墳（平凡社、刊行後版）|2006}}。墳丘は2段築成で、厚さ10センチメートル程度の[[版築]]状の水平積み上げによって構築される{{Sfn|三津屋古墳（平凡社、刊行後版）|2006}}。墳丘外表には[[葺石]]が認められるほか、墳丘周囲には周濠が巡らされる。埋葬施設は両袖式の[[横穴式石室]]で、玄室奥壁を八角形の中心として南方向に開口する。石室は大きく破壊を受けているが、自然石乱石積みによって構築されて一部には切石を使用したと見られ、前面には前庭部を付す{{Sfn|三津屋古墳（平凡社、刊行後版）|2006}}。盗掘のため副葬品は詳らかでない。 この三津屋古墳は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]後半頃の築造と推定される。八角墳は[[段ノ塚古墳]]（[[奈良県]][[桜井市]]、[[舒明天皇]]陵）・[[御廟野古墳]]（[[京都府]][[京都市]]、[[天智天皇]]陵）・[[野口王墓|野口王墓古墳]]（奈良県[[明日香村]]、[[天武天皇|天武]]・[[持統天皇]]合葬陵）など当時の[[天皇陵]]クラスの古墳で採用される墳丘形態であり、当地の豪族の特異性を示す点で貴重な古墳になる。また本古墳の北西にある[[南下古墳群]]は上毛野地域において総社古墳群（[[前橋市]]）に次ぐ有力首長墓群であり、本古墳と合わせて畿内[[ヤマト王権]]による上毛野地域の中央集権化との関係を考察するうえで重要視される右島和夫「記念講演 古墳から見た七世紀の上毛野地域 -吉岡町南下古墳群を中心として-」『群馬文化』第338号、群馬県地域文化研究協議会、2019年。。 古墳域は[[1995年]]（平成7年）に群馬県指定史跡に指定されている。 == 遺跡歴 == * [[1993年]]（[[平成]]5年）、発掘調査（吉岡町教育委員会、[[1996年]]に報告書刊行）。 * [[1995年]]（平成7年）3月24日、群馬県指定史跡に指定。 * [[2001年]]（平成13年）3月23日、史跡範囲の追加指定。 == 墳丘 == 古墳の規模は、対角長約23.8メートル・残存高さ4.5メートルを測り、八角形の一辺は下段約9メートル・上段約6メートルを測る。築造に際しては1尺約30センチメートルの唐尺の使用が推測される。 墳丘の葺石には、下段では山石が、上段では扁平な川原石が使用されており、特に上段は精巧な造りになる。 == 文化財 == === 群馬県指定文化財 === * 史跡 ** 三津屋古墳 - 1995年（平成7年）3月24日指定、2001年（平成13年）3月23日追加指定[https://www.net.yoshioka.ed.jp/%e6%8c%87%e5%ae%9a%e6%96%87%e5%8c%96%e8%b2%a1/%e4%b8%89%e6%b4%a5%e5%b1%8b%e5%8f%a4%e5%a2%b3 三津屋古墳]（吉岡町教育委員会）。史跡説明板。。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用した文献）}} * 史跡説明板（吉岡町教育委員会、2021年設置） * [http://www.net.yoshioka.ed.jp/%E5%90%89%E5%B2%A1%E7%94%BA%E6%96%87%E5%8C%96%E8%B2%A1%E3%82%BB%E3%83%B3%E3%82%BF%E3%83%BC-1/%E3%83%91%E3%83%B3%E3%83%95%E3%83%AC%E3%83%83%E3%83%88%E3%83%BB%E5%8B%95%E7%94%BB/?action=common_download_main&upload_id=4439 三津屋古墳パンフレット]（吉岡町教育委員会、2021年） - リンクは吉岡町教育委員会。 * {{Cite book|和書|author1=大塚初重|authorlink1=大塚初重|author2=柳下恵理子|year=|chapter=三津屋古墳|title=[[日本大百科全書]]（ニッポニカ）|publisher=[[小学館]]|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|三津屋古墳（日本大百科全書）}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=荒木勇次|year=2002|chapter=三津屋古墳|title=[[日本古墳大辞典|続 日本古墳大辞典]]|publisher=[[東京堂出版]]|isbn=4490105991|ref={{Harvid|三津屋古墳（続古墳）|2002}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=2006|chapter=三津屋古墳|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 10 群馬県の地名 刊行後版（[[ジャパンナレッジ]]収録）|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=4582490107|ref={{Harvid|三津屋古墳（平凡社、刊行後版）|2006}}}} == 関連文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用していない関連文献）}} * {{Cite book|和書|year=1996|title=三津屋古墳 -八角形墳の調査-（吉岡町文化財調査報告書 第7集）|publisher=吉岡町教育委員会|ref=}} == 関連項目 == * [[南下古墳群]] * [[三宮神社 (吉岡町)]] == 外部リンク == {{Commonscat|Mitsuya Kofun}} * [https://www.net.yoshioka.ed.jp/%e6%8c%87%e5%ae%9a%e6%96%87%e5%8c%96%e8%b2%a1/%e4%b8%89%e6%b4%a5%e5%b1%8b%e5%8f%a4%e5%a2%b3 三津屋古墳] - [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of [[:en:Mount Haruna|Mount Haruna]], near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the [[:en:Japanese imperial tombs|Japanese imperial tombs]]. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of [[:en:Mount Haruna|Mount Haruna]], near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the [[:en:Japanese imperial tombs|Japanese imperial tombs]]. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of [[:en:Mount Haruna|Mount Haruna]], near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the [[:en:Japanese imperial tombs|Japanese imperial tombs]]. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of [[:en:Mount Haruna|Mount Haruna]], near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the [[:en:Japanese imperial tombs|Japanese imperial tombs]]. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of [[:en:Mount Haruna|Mount Haruna]], near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the [[:en:Japanese imperial tombs|Japanese imperial tombs]]. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of [[:en:Mount Haruna|Mount Haruna]], near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the [[:en:Japanese imperial tombs|Japanese imperial tombs]]. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of [[:en:Mount Haruna|Mount Haruna]], near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the [[:en:Japanese imperial tombs|Japanese imperial tombs]]. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of [[:en:Mount Haruna|Mount Haruna]], near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the [[:en:Japanese imperial tombs|Japanese imperial tombs]]. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of [[:en:Mount Haruna|Mount Haruna]], near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the [[:en:Japanese imperial tombs|Japanese imperial tombs]]. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of [[:en:Mount Haruna|Mount Haruna]], near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the [[:en:Japanese imperial tombs|Japanese imperial tombs]]. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of [[:en:Mount Haruna|Mount Haruna]], near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the [[:en:Japanese imperial tombs|Japanese imperial tombs]]. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of [[:en:Mount Haruna|Mount Haruna]], near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the [[:en:Japanese imperial tombs|Japanese imperial tombs]]. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun:
