[[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of [[:en:Mount Haruna|Mount Haruna]], near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the [[:en:Japanese imperial tombs|Japanese imperial tombs]]. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of [[:en:Mount Haruna|Mount Haruna]], near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the [[:en:Japanese imperial tombs|Japanese imperial tombs]]. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of [[:en:Mount Haruna|Mount Haruna]], near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the [[:en:Japanese imperial tombs|Japanese imperial tombs]]. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of [[:en:Mount Haruna|Mount Haruna]], near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the [[:en:Japanese imperial tombs|Japanese imperial tombs]]. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of [[:en:Mount Haruna|Mount Haruna]], near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the [[:en:Japanese imperial tombs|Japanese imperial tombs]]. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of [[:en:Mount Haruna|Mount Haruna]], near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the [[:en:Japanese imperial tombs|Japanese imperial tombs]]. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of [[:en:Mount Haruna|Mount Haruna]], near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the [[:en:Japanese imperial tombs|Japanese imperial tombs]]. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: Haruna|Mount Haruna]], near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the [[:en:Japanese imperial tombs|Japanese imperial tombs]]. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of [[:en:Mount Haruna|Mount Haruna]], near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the [[:en:Japanese imperial tombs|Japanese imperial tombs]]. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|en|Mount Haruna|WD=Q1191690|lt=Mount Haruna}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Japanese imperial tombs|en|Japanese imperial tombs|WD=Q17218816|lt=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|en|Mount Haruna|WD=Q1191690|lt=Mount Haruna}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Japanese imperial tombs|en|Japanese imperial tombs|WD=Q17218816|lt=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|en|Mount Haruna|WD=Q1191690|lt=Mount Haruna}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Japanese imperial tombs|en|Japanese imperial tombs|WD=Q17218816|lt=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|en|Mount Haruna|WD=Q1191690|lt=Mount Haruna}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Japanese imperial tombs|en|Japanese imperial tombs|WD=Q17218816|lt=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: It is Historic Site1 as a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mitsuya Kofun|qq=}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is an {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|comment=enwiki is a |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150907095743/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=31732 |archive-date=2015-09-07 }} A rare kind of tomb mostly reserved for |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 |access-date=2023-10-20}}.{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Kofun, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Kofun |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal Kofun said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}}, The inner chamber is open to the public. unlike many other Kofun which are strictly restricted by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}} [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|en|Mount Haruna|WD=Q1191690|lt=Mount Haruna}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Japanese imperial tombs|en|Japanese imperial tombs|WD=Q17218816|lt=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|en|Mount Haruna|WD=Q1191690|lt=Mount Haruna|1=Mount Haruna}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century|1=7th century}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Japanese imperial tombs|en|Japanese imperial tombs|WD=Q17218816|lt=Japanese imperial tombs|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|en|Mount Haruna|WD=Q1191690|lt=Mount Haruna|1=Mount Haruna}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century|1=7th century}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Japanese imperial tombs|en|Japanese imperial tombs|WD=Q17218816|lt=Japanese imperial tombs|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|en|Mount Haruna|WD=Q1191690|lt=Mount Haruna|1=Mount Haruna}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century|1=7th century}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Japanese imperial tombs|en|Japanese imperial tombs|WD=Q17218816|lt=Japanese imperial tombs|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}}, The inner chamber is open to the public. unlike many other Kofun which are strictly restricted by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|the entrance of the Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|en|Mount Haruna|WD=Q1191690|lt=Mount Haruna|1=Mount Haruna}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century|1=7th century}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Japanese imperial tombs|en|Japanese imperial tombs|WD=Q17218816|lt=Japanese imperial tombs|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun: Kofun]] == Overview == [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, funkyu from behind.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kofun}}]] [[File:Mitsuya Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber}}]] Mitsuya Kofun is located on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Haruna|en|Mount Haruna|qid=Q1191690|lt=Mount Haruna|1=Mount Haruna}}, near the left bank of the Gōōzu River, a tributary of the Tone River. Excavation in 1993 revealed its unique octagonal type. The tumulus is two-tiered, constructed using a rammed-earth technique. The outer surface is covered with stones, and a surrounding moat is present. The burial facility features a bilateral entry horizontal stone chamber, with the rear wall typeing an octagonal focal point that opens southward. Although the chamber is heavily damaged, it is constructed with natural and dressed stones. The absence of burial goods is attributed to looting. Mitsuya Kofun dates back to the late {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|qid=Q8089|lt=7th century|1=7th century}} and represents the distinctive octagonal tumulus style associated with imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Japanese imperial tombs|en|Japanese imperial tombs|qid=Q17218816|lt=Japanese imperial tombs|1=Japanese imperial tombs}}. Its unique design highlights the influence of the Yamato administration in the Kōzuke region. == Historical Significance == * In 1993, an excavation was conducted, with findings published in 1996. * On March 24, 1995, the kofun was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site. * The site boundaries were expanded on March 23, 2001. == Kofun Features == The tumulus measures 23.8 meters diagonally and stands 4.5 meters tall. Its octagonal base measures approximately 9 meters on the lower tier and 6 meters on the upper tier. Stone coverings on the lower tier use mountain stones, while the upper tier features flat river stones. == Historic Site == === Gunma Prefectural designation1 === * Historic Site ''' Mitsuya Kofun:
